value.rationale: V: A systematic third-derivative mechanism yields an interval, not one arbitrary stationary point, where the actual published four-choice safeguarded derivative-free algorithm cannot advance on strongly convex smooth objectives. The attained r^4 objective obstruction explains the order-necessity of the paper′s epsilon^(1/4) radius rule, with explicit coefficients and an all-r analytic test family; this gives a nontrivial boundary for radius scheduling and algorithmic safeguarding rather than routine finite-difference error rephrasing.
